verdict: Skydo's most-fetched blog post is not a blog post. It is the product landing page served at a /blog URL: same calculator, same carousel, same eleven CTAs. ChatGPT fetches it 1,151 times because the URL and title match the query, then quotes it once in seven fetches. Roarbank's plain guide on the same topic is quoted 1.2 times per fetch.

diagnosis: The blog is the landing page. The HTML at /blog/how-to-receive-international-payments-in-india is identical to /receive-international-payments-in-india. ChatGPT fetches it as a guide and finds a product page.
How-to answers have a fixed shape: numbered method, how it works, fees, time, then tips and compliance. Roarbank's page is already in that shape, so each block maps to a sentence in the answer.
Steps beat cards. The single most-lifted unit is the 'How does it work?' bullet list under each method. Skydo's cards have no steps at all.
A requirements checklist and a tips list are the cheapest citations on the page. Roarbank has both; Skydo has neither as a list.
Fee tables need text headers and a date or disclaimer. Roarbank's six-row fee tables are quoted; Skydo's logo-header table is invisible.
Brand balance signals a guide. Roarbank names four platforms roughly equally and its own once. Skydo names itself 42 times and gives Stripe three lines.
One CTA. Roarbank's only pitch is a banner. Skydo's eleven CTAs break every block ChatGPT would otherwise quote whole.
Short and specific wins the rate. SME Advisory's 709-word signed guide with codes and section numbers is cited 1.41 times per fetch, the best rate of any editorial page in the window.
spec: Give the blog URL its own article. Do not serve the landing page template at /blog. Keep the landing page for product intent; the blog is for the how-to query.
H1 as the question, date and author under it, Article plus Person schema.
Intro: two paragraphs, who it is for and what it covers. No calculator, no badges.
Key takeaways: 5 bullets, one per method plus one selection rule.
Before you start: 5-6 bullet checklist (Indian bank account, SWIFT/BIC, PAN, GST registration, invoice, purpose code).

Methods as numbered H3s, 6 of them: SWIFT, PayPal, Wise, Payoneer, payment gateways (Razorpay, Cashfree), Skydo. Each with the same four sub-blocks: one-paragraph description; 'How it works' 3-5 bullets; 'Fees' mini-table with Fee type / Approximate cost / Notes and an 'as of <month> 2026' line; 'Time to receive' 2 bullets. Skydo is one method among six with its real numbers, not 'Recommended'.
Comparison table with text headers: Method / Best for / Typical cost / Time / FIRA.
How to choose: 6 bullets with bolded leads keyed to amount, fees, speed, client convenience, documentation, frequency.
Compliance section with codes and numbers: purpose code (P0802, P0807), FIRC vs FIRA, AD bank, GST LUT, realisation window, each linking to the reference page.
FAQ: 4-6 questions as headings, two-sentence factual answers, FAQPage schema.
Length 1,500-2,000 words. No paragraph over 60 words. 40-60 bullets. One CTA at the end.
Success check after 30 days: citations per fetch above 0.6 on this URL (today 0.15) and the page cited on how-to prompts, not only price prompts.

playbook.use_when: The query starts with 'how to' or 'how can I' and expects a set of methods or steps: receive international payments, get paid from a country, invoice a foreign client, open an account.
blueprint: Title and H1 are the question itself, with 'in India' and the year in the title tag.
Byline with author name, credential, date and read time. Article and Person schema.
Intro in two paragraphs: the reader types this is for, and the scope. Nothing about the brand.
Key takeaways block: 5 bullets, one per method, plus one rule for choosing.
Before-you-start checklist: 5-6 bullets of documents and prerequisites.

Methods as numbered H3s under one H2. Same four sub-blocks every time: description paragraph, 'How it works' 3-5 bullets, fees mini-table with text headers and a date, time-to-receive 2 bullets. Name real platforms with real numbers under each method. Skydo is one entry, with its own numbers and its own cons.
One comparison table with text headers: Method / Best for / Cost / Time / FIRA.
How-to-choose list: 6 bullets with a bolded lead phrase each.
Compliance section with codes, forms and windows, linking to the reference pages rather than re-explaining.
FAQ of 4-6 questions as headings, two-sentence factual answers, FAQPage schema.
1,500-2,000 words. Paragraphs under 40 words on average, none over 60. 40-60 bullets. One CTA, at the end.
Never reuse a landing-page template for a blog URL. No calculators, carousels, logo-header tables or repeated badges.
